criteria_results.title: IP section revised from ownership to perpetual-license construct
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline deletes Customer ownership of Customer-Trained Adaptations and replaces it with Vendor ownership plus an irrevocable, perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid-up license for Customer to access, use, reproduce, deploy, modify, and further develop the fine-tuned adaptations, including post-termination export rights for adapter weights.

criteria_results.title: Non-assertion covenant included in IP section
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 includes Section 5.3, a broad Vendor non-assertion covenant covering patents, copyrights, trade secrets, trademarks, and other IP rights, and protecting Customer’s post-termination use, deployment, modification, and further development of the exported Customer-Trained Adaptations.

criteria_results.title: API-based weight export portability within 30 days in industry-standard format
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly requires an API-based export of all fine-tuned adapter weights within 30 days after expiration or termination, in an industry-standard format such as ONNX, SafeTensors, or a mutually agreed equivalent. This appears in Section 5.2 and is reinforced in Section 13.6(g).

criteria_results.title: Escrow provisions included as part of IP protective measures
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 includes escrow as part of the IP protection framework accompanying the perpetual license. Article 5A requires deposit of Customer’s fine-tuned adapter weights, related training/configuration and pipeline artifacts, documentation, and manifests; provides update, verification, release-trigger, and post-release license terms; and is supplemented by Exhibit E. Section 5.2 also grants the perpetual license and export rights, while the issues list expressly identifies escrow as one of the protections conditioning that license structure.

criteria_results.title: General liability cap at 1.5× annual fees ($3,600,000)
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 Section 10.2 sets the general aggregate liability cap at 1.5 times the $2,400,000 Annual Platform Fee, expressly equal to $3,600,000.

criteria_results.title: Super-cap at 3× annual fees ($7,200,000) for IP indemnity and data-breach carve-outs
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 10.3 applies a three-times annual-fee super-cap of $7,200,000 to both Vendor’s Article 6/data-breach liability and its IP indemnification obligations under Section 11.1 (as well as Section 11.2).

criteria_results.title: Willful misconduct and gross negligence remain fully uncapped
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 10.3 expressly provides that liability arising from either party’s willful misconduct or gross negligence is uncapped and reiterates that no limitation or cap applies to either. The issues list also accurately states that these liabilities remain uncapped.

criteria_results.title: CCPA service-provider designation and certification
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly requires Vendor to act solely as a CCPA service provider/processor, not an independent controller. Section 6.2 cites Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(ag) and requires certification in the DPA, while Exhibit D, Section 3 contains the service-provider certification and applicable CCPA/CPRA restrictions.

criteria_results.title: Prohibition on use of Customer Data for model improvement with de-identification conditions
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly prohibits using Customer Data for model improvement unless the data is de-identified and aggregated in compliance with Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(m), and the methodology is independently verified in writing by a third-party assessor approved by Customer before use. Sections 6.1 and DPA Sections 4A and 5 state these requirements as specific contractual obligations and prohibit re-identification.

criteria_results.title: Uptime SLA at 99.95% monthly
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 sets the Platform availability requirement at 99.95% in Section 9.1 and repeats the same monthly uptime target in Exhibit B. The updated issues list also accurately identifies the 99.95% monthly uptime SLA as resolved.

criteria_results.title: Uptime SLA exclusions for scheduled maintenance and force majeure
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly excludes qualifying scheduled maintenance windows and Force Majeure Events from uptime Downtime calculations in Section 9.1 and Exhibit B. It also specifies the agreed scheduled-maintenance conditions, including 72 hours’ advance notice and a four-hour monthly limit.

criteria_results.title: Latency SLA at p95 ≤ 450 ms in Draft 3
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 sets the API latency SLA at the 95th percentile to p95 ≤ 450 ms in Section 9.2 and consistently reflects that target in Exhibit B.

criteria_results.title: Issues list flags latency as yellow-zone item (450 ms vs. product team's 400 ms preference)
criteria_results.reasoning: The issues list identifies the latency SLA as p95 ≤ 450 ms, marks it as a yellow-zone caution, and expressly notes that Product Engineering/Priya prefers sub-400 ms latency for LendStream real-time decisioning.

criteria_results.title: F1 accuracy threshold at ≥ 0.92 initial
criteria_results.reasoning: Although Section 9.3 and the SOW set the stabilization-period F1 threshold at ≥0.92, Exhibit B still states that the initial Stabilization Period target is ≥0.90. This conflicting initial threshold fails the requirement that Draft 3 use ≥0.92.

criteria_results.title: F1 ramp mechanism to ≥ 0.94 after 90-day stabilization period post-Go-Live
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly requires F1 ≥ 0.92 during the 90-day stabilization period following the October 1, 2025 Go-Live and increases the target to F1 ≥ 0.94 beginning January 1, 2026 and thereafter. This satisfies the required post-stabilization ramp mechanism.

criteria_results.title: SLA service credits capped at 20% of monthly fees ($40,000)
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly caps aggregate SLA Service Credits at 20% of the $200,000 monthly Annual Platform Fee installment, equal to $40,000 per month, in Section 9.4 and Exhibit B Section 5(c).

criteria_results.title: Termination right for 3 consecutive months of SLA miss retained
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 retains Section 9.5, allowing Customer to terminate on 30 days’ written notice if Vendor misses any SLA target for three or more consecutive calendar months. The same trigger is also preserved in Exhibit B.

criteria_results.title: New AI-output indemnity provision inserted
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 inserts a new Section 11.2, “AI-Output Indemnification,” requiring Vendor to defend, indemnify, and hold Customer harmless from third-party claims alleging that AI-generated Platform outputs infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights or violate applicable law.

criteria_results.title: AI-output indemnity carve-out for Customer modification or off-label use
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 11.2 includes the required carve-out: the AI-output indemnity does not apply to claims to the extent caused by Customer’s modification of an output after receipt or Customer’s use of the Platform or output outside the documented use case in the SOW.

criteria_results.title: IP indemnity scope broadened to all intellectual property rights
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 broadens Section 11.1 beyond registered U.S. patents and copyrights. It covers Customer’s authorized use of the Platform and expressly includes patents, copyrights, trade secrets, trademarks, moral rights, rights of publicity, database rights, and analogous foreign-law rights worldwide.

criteria_results.title: Escrow of adapter weights plus training configuration and pipeline artifacts
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3’s operative redline requires escrow of all Customer fine-tuned adapter weights plus the training configuration and pipeline artifacts needed to reproduce, redeploy, or use them, including scripts, hyperparameters, serving configurations, dependencies, and documentation. It expressly excludes the Base Model source code and Vendor’s general-purpose training infrastructure.

criteria_results.title: Iron Mountain IPM as proposed escrow agent with NCC Group as acceptable alternative
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 names Iron Mountain Intellectual Property Management, Inc. as the proposed Escrow Agent, and the updated issues list expressly identifies NCC Group plc as an acceptable Yellow fallback.

criteria_results.title: Escrow release triggers include insolvency, material uncured breach (>60 days), and cessation of product support
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 5A.3 includes all three required escrow release triggers: Vendor insolvency/bankruptcy, a material breach remaining uncured for more than 60 days after notice, and cessation or announced discontinuation of Platform support or availability.

criteria_results.title: Tech E&O insurance accepted at $5M per occurrence in Draft 3
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3, Section 12.1(b), sets Technology Errors & Omissions / Cyber Liability Insurance at $5,000,000 per occurrence, satisfying the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Issues list flags Tech E&O as yellow-zone item (playbook prefers $10M for TCV > $5M)
criteria_results.reasoning: Issue 11 flags the $5M Tech E&O limit as a “YELLOW-ZONE CAUTION” and expressly states that $10M is preferred for TCV above $5M, noting this deal’s $7.2M platform-fee TCV.

criteria_results.title: Delaware governing law maintained in Draft 3
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 maintains Delaware governing law in Section 14.1, which states that the Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware. No other state's law is specified as governing law.

criteria_results.title: Delaware courts (Court of Chancery or U.S. District Court for D. Del.) as dispute forum
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 14.2 specifies exclusive dispute resolution in the Delaware Court of Chancery or, if that court declines jurisdiction, the Delaware Superior Court or the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware. It does not require arbitration and includes the required Delaware federal forum.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes CCPA service-provider certification language
criteria_results.reasoning: Exhibit D, Section 3 expressly certifies that Vendor is a “service provider” under Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(ag) and includes the associated restrictions on selling, sharing, retaining, using, disclosing, and combining Customer Data. The main agreement also references this DPA and certification in Sections 6.2 and 6.8.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes GLBA safeguards compliance
criteria_results.reasoning: The Draft 3 DPA expressly addresses GLBA safeguards compliance. Exhibit D, Section 4 states that Customer Data includes consumer NPPI subject to GLBA and requires Vendor to comply with all applicable safeguard requirements. The main data-processing provisions also reference GLBA and the FTC Safeguards Rule and impose specific security controls.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes 72-hour data breach notification
criteria_results.reasoning: Exhibit D, Section 8 requires Vendor to notify Customer of any confirmed or reasonably suspected Security Breach within seventy-two (72) hours after Vendor first becomes aware of it, consistent with the required timeline.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes sub-processor management with prior written consent
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly requires Customer’s prior written consent before Vendor may engage any sub-processor, both in Section 6.6 of the Agreement and Section 6 of Exhibit D (DPA).

criteria_results.title: DPA includes de-identification standards with statutory compliance and independent verification
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 requires de-identification to comply with the statutory CCPA standard in Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(m) and requires written verification by an independent third-party assessor approved by Customer before any model-improvement use. These requirements appear in the DPA, including Sections 4A and 5.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes data return/deletion upon termination
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly addresses post-termination data return and deletion. DPA Section 10 requires Vendor, upon termination or expiration, to return or delete all Customer Data in accordance with Agreement Section 6.7 within 30 days of Customer’s written request and certify completion in writing.

criteria_results.title: Issues list covers all 12 minimum negotiation point categories
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list covers all 12 required categories: IP ownership/licensing (#5), liability cap (#6), data processing/de-identification (#8), uptime SLA (#1), latency SLA (#2), accuracy/F1 SLA (#3), SLA credits (#4), escrow (#13), AI-output indemnity (#9), IP indemnity scope (#10), Tech E&O insurance (#11), and governing law/dispute resolution (#12).

criteria_results.title: IP ownership/licensing categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes “IP ownership / license structure (perpetual license, portability, escrow, non-assertion)” as “Partially Resolved,” noting that the perpetual-license construct is accepted subject to protective conditions and that ownership remains preferred.

criteria_results.title: Liability cap categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes the liability cap as “Open,” which is expressly acceptable under the criterion because the proposed 1.5× compromise has not been accepted by Meridian. It is not categorized as fully resolved.

criteria_results.title: Data processing/de-identification categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes item 8, “Data processing / CCPA service-provider and de-identified data,” as “Partially Resolved,” while identifying the de-identification conditions as mandatory proposed requirements rather than fully agreed terms.

criteria_results.title: Uptime SLA categorized as resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes “Uptime SLA (99.95% monthly)” as “Resolved” and identifies the agreed scheduled-maintenance and Force Majeure exclusions.

criteria_results.title: Latency SLA categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes the latency SLA as “Partially Resolved,” states that Draft 3 accepts p95 latency of 450 ms, and expressly notes that Product Engineering/Priya prefers sub-400 ms performance.

criteria_results.title: Accuracy/F1 SLA categorized as open
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes “Accuracy / F1 score (0.92 ramp to 0.94)” as “Open” and states that Meridian has not agreed to the proposed ramp.

criteria_results.title: SLA credits categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes “SLA credits (20% cap / $40,000 per month)” as “Open,” not fully resolved. This satisfies the criterion, which permits either “Open” or “Partially Resolved.”

criteria_results.title: Escrow categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes escrow (item 13) as “Open,” noting that the agent, scope, and related terms remain unaccepted. The criterion expressly permits either “Partially Resolved” or “Open” and only fails if escrow is marked fully “Resolved.”

criteria_results.title: AI-output indemnity categorized as open
criteria_results.reasoning: In the updated negotiation issues list, item 9, “AI-output indemnity (new provision),” is expressly categorized as “Open,” consistent with Meridian not having substantively responded.

criteria_results.title: IP indemnity scope categorized as open
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes “IP indemnity scope (all IP rights / authorized use)” as “Open” and explains that Draft 3 proposes broader coverage that has not yet been agreed by Meridian.

criteria_results.title: Tech E&O insurance categorized as partially resolved with yellow-zone flag
criteria_results.reasoning: In the updated issues list, item 11 (“Insurance / Tech E&O ($5M accepted)”) is categorized as “Partially Resolved” and expressly marked “YELLOW-ZONE CAUTION,” satisfying both requirements.

criteria_results.title: Governing law/dispute resolution categorized as open
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes item 12, “Governing law / dispute resolution,” as “Open” and expressly notes that the issue remains fully open with no email movement.

criteria_results.title: Draft 3 is redlined against Draft 2 as the base (not Draft 1)
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 contains tracked insertions and deletions, and the companion issues list expressly identifies Draft 2—with its prior changes accepted—as the clean redline base. The displayed revisions reflect subsequent Draft 3 changes rather than a redline against Draft 1.

criteria_results.title: Annual platform fee preserved at $2,400,000/yr
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 preserves the Annual Platform Fee at $2,400,000 per Contract Year in Section 4.1, with corresponding monthly installments of $200,000 and a three-year total of $7,200,000.

criteria_results.title: 3-year initial term preserved (July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2028)
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 preserves the three-year Initial Term. Section 13.1 states that it begins on July 1, 2025 and expires on June 30, 2028, and the Initial Term definition is consistent with those dates.

criteria_results.title: Implementation fee preserved at $850,000 with 50/50 milestone split
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 preserves the one-time implementation fee at $850,000 and splits it into two equal $425,000 installments: the first upon execution of the Initial SOW and the second upon Go-Live. This is reflected in Section 4.2 and Exhibit A.

criteria_results.title: Included API calls preserved at 40,000,000/yr with $0.012 overage
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 preserves 40,000,000 included API calls per Contract Year and an overage rate of $0.012 per API call in Section 4.3; the definitions and updated issues list are consistent with those terms.

criteria_results.title: 180-day auto-renewal notice period preserved
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 13.2 preserves automatic renewal for successive 12-month terms unless either party gives at least 180 days’ prior notice of non-renewal. The updated issues list also confirms the 180-day non-renewal notice.

criteria_results.title: Issues list notes latency 450 ms is within playbook acceptable range but below preferred 400 ms
criteria_results.reasoning: Issue 2 identifies p95 ≤450 ms as accepted, notes Product Engineering/Priya’s preference for sub-400 ms due to LendStream real-time decisioning, and states that ≤500 ms is the fallback ceiling subject to Product confirmation. This supplies the required acceptable-range, preferred-target, and product-experience context.

criteria_results.title: Issues list recommends considering latency escalation at the May 19 joint call
criteria_results.reasoning: The latency issue entry expressly recommends revisiting the p95 ≤450 ms position at the week-of-May-19 joint call, while noting Product Engineering’s preference for sub-400 ms. This satisfies the requirement to recommend considering escalation at that call.

criteria_results.title: Issues list flags AI-output indemnity as fully open with no Meridian response
criteria_results.reasoning: The issues list marks AI-output indemnity as “Open,” but it does not state that Meridian has not substantively responded or that Delacroix acknowledged the issue on May 9 and said Meridian needed internal review.

criteria_results.title: Issues list notes playbook fallback for AI-output indemnity (shared-risk with vendor first-dollar coverage)
criteria_results.reasoning: The issues list expressly states under AI-output indemnity: “Playbook fallback: shared-risk framework with Meridian first-dollar defense, settlement, and judgment coverage up to the negotiated cap/super-cap,” satisfying the criterion.
